newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's King Simeon urges coalition government.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's King Simeon urges coalition government.

text.p: Bulgaria's King Simeon returned to his homeland on Tuesday to appeal to political forces contesting Saturday's elections to unite in a broad coalition to push forward badly-needed economic reforms.
Simeon urged voters to turn out to support the reforms, which he said were essential to attract foreign investment and integrate Bulgaria with the European mainstream.
"Political pluralism is more appropriate to Bulgaria than the two-party Anglo-Saxon model," the bearded monarch told a ceremony commemorating Bulgaria's first constitution.
Simeon received a rapturous welcome from thousands of supporters in the northern town of Veliko Tarnovo, where the 1879 law calling for a constitutional monarchy was drafted.

"We all suffered in the past from the rule of a single party, be that good or bad. I am not a political leader and my function is not to bless one political force or chastise another," he told a news conference in the mountain village of Arbanassy after the ceremony.
"It is up to the political forces to decide and negotiate how they would form a coalition. This is an issue of balance and maximal representation of all Bulgarians in the government."

The main monarchist parties contested the last elections in coalition with the centre-right Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), which is expected to win a majority on Saturday, but this time several have formed an alliance with the ethnic Turks' Movement for Rights and Freedoms.
UDF spokeswoman Nadezhda Mihailova, who attended the ceremony, said the King's speech had raised many serious issues and the UDF welcomed his visit.

"These elections will show how much weight each political force has. The configuration of the next parliament will open the way for discussion on future coalitions. We are open for a broad discussion," she said.

Simeon flew with a special plane to an airfield near Veliko Tarnovo, once capital of the Second Bulgarian Kingdom which existed between 1185 and 1396, when its medieval civilisation was wiped out by the Ottoman Turks.

The 59-year-old King will spend the night in Arbanassy at a residence built by former communist dictator Todor Zhivkov and fly to Sofia on Wednesday for lunch with reformist president Petar Stoyanov before returning to Madrid.
Simeon went into exile as a child in 1946 when the Soviet army installed a communist regime and returned for the first time for a three-week visit last May.
Tuesday's speech, his most outspoken political intervention yet, included an attack on misrepresentation of his position by politicians and journalists.

"Attempts by many people to use my name...as well as implausible speculation, made me come here today in order that you may hear clearly from me in my mother tongue what concerns me," said the balding, bearded monarch.

"Those who think that Simeon divides Bulgarians into Monarchists and Republicans, Left and Right, are wrong, as I am stretching out my hand to everyone. I am interested in what unites us, not what divides us. Patriots can be found in every camp," he said in a speech frequently interrupted with applause and chants of "Simeon, Simeon".
"I am appealing to everyone to vote. Vote for implementation of reforms and thereby for the integration of the country into the European structures," he said.
